title: mcmt extract document
description: Layer 3 (rule tagging) output, consumed by Layer 4 (translation) and Layer 5 (output backends). SCHEMA_VERSION 3. There is no backwards compatibility: a document whose schema_version does not equal the tool's SCHEMA_VERSION is rejected outright.

schema_version.description: Single version number shared by all four mcmt contracts. Mismatch is a fatal error, never a migration.

rule_set_version.description: Version of the rule pack. Changing it changes which nodes are extracted, so it participates in extract_fingerprint.

namespace.description: Single custom lang-key namespace. MUST NOT be 'minecraft'.

world_fingerprint.description: Identity of the scanned world snapshot. MUST be derived from per-chunk DataVersions and region content, NOT from file mtime or size: [實測] opening a world in-game upgraded 182 of 120,036 chunks with no meaningful mtime signal.

extract_fingerprint.description: Identity of THIS extract document: hash over world_fingerprint + rule_set_version + namespace + the sorted unit_id list. Two extracts of the same world with different rule_set_version have the same world_fingerprint but different extract_fingerprint. translations.json binds to this, not to world_fingerprint alone.

skipped_unparseable.description: Nodes that looked like legacy JSON but failed to parse. These are counted and reported, never silently treated as literal text.

skipped_legacy_json_in_native_chunk.description: Legacy JSON-shaped nodes found in a chunk whose data_version is >= 4325. [遊戲實測 M0-3/M0-4] the game does not JSON-parse a TAG_String in a native chunk, it renders it literally, so these are display garbage rather than content. Translating them would write back a string that still renders as garbage; v1 excludes them and reports the count.

discriminator.description: 16 hex chars = 64 bits of blake2b, optionally followed by _<n> when a collision or a manual disambiguation forced a split. 40 bits was inadequate: at 50k entries its collision probability is ~11%, and the scan corpus includes 2,613 mcfunctions and 692 command blocks.

unitId.description: u:<category>:<discriminator>. The discriminator here and the discriminator inside translateKey are THE SAME STRING, produced once by one function. They never diverge.

translateKey.description: <namespace>.<category>.<discriminator>[.<segment_index>]. The optional trailing .<n> is the SEGMENT INDEX, present only when unit.collapsible is false and the backend must emit one key per text segment. Collision/disambiguation lives inside the discriminator as _<n>, never in the trailing segment slot.

category.description: hover_text covers components nested inside hover_event (MP2 has 331 such nodes under book pages). Included in scan scope by decision.

key.description: Base key WITHOUT a segment index. Non-null iff strategy is translate_key. When collapsible is false the backend derives per-segment keys by appending .<i>.

collapsible.description: True iff the whole component tree can be replaced by ONE {translate: key} node without losing anything: every segment's style is expressible as legacy § codes, and the tree contains no translate/score/selector/keybind/nbt/click_event/hover_event/insertion/font node. When false the backend MUST rebuild the tree and emit one key per segment. [實測] 2,261 translatable component trees in Minecraft Party 2 carry an extra array; 84% of them have children with their own formatting, and the deepest observed nesting is 3.

flags.description: already_target_language is set by a cheap CJK-ratio heuristic in layer 3 so the translation layer can skip text that is already in the target language. Real adventure maps are routinely mixed-language and this materially cuts token spend at 989 MB scale.

then.description: [遊戲實測] These fields only accept a literal string. A translate key placed in book title.raw renders the raw key on screen. block_entity_name joined the list on 2026-08-21 [遊戲實測 M11-3]: an SNBT translate component written into a native chunk's CustomName renders as literal text in the container GUI, exactly as sign messages[] do (M0-3). in_place here means the writer replaces the text INSIDE the node while KEEPING the node's existing NBT shape; it does not promote a TAG_String to a compound, because that promotion has never been tested for this field.
plain_string means the field is not a component at all. Machine-enforced, not merely documented.
A non-collapsible tree needs per-segment keys, which the in_place strategy has no way to express.

source.description: The unit's text, flattened out of the component tree. § codes and structural formatting are NOT two separate mechanisms: both become segments, and both are marked in `text` by the same [[n]] token.

text.description: ★ THE HASH INPUT and what the translator reads. The literal text of the ENTIRE component tree (recursing through extra, and through hover_event when in scope) flattened into render order. When the tree has TWO OR MORE style segments, a [[n]] token marks the start of each; n counts from 0 and indexes `segments`. When there is exactly ONE segment -- the overwhelming majority of real nodes -- NO token is emitted at all and `text` equals `plain`, because a marker that appears on every line is noise a human editor has to work around and can silently delete. A translation MUST preserve the exact multiset of [[n]] tokens it was given.

plain.description: text with all [[n]] tokens removed. Display and width measurement only; never round-tripped.

segments.description: segments[n] describes segment n. With two or more segments each is opened by a [[n]] token in `text`; with exactly one there is no token and the single segment covers the whole string. Style VALUES are per-occurrence (see occurrence.segment_styles); this array carries only the kind and the sigma-expressibility, which are what determine unit identity and collapsibility.

escaped_literals.description: Present when the ORIGINAL text contained a literal [[n]]-shaped substring. Those are escaped to [[\n]] in `text`; this array records the originals in order so unmasking can restore them. Pairs with the contains_placeholder_like_text flag.

kind.description: none: unstyled run. legacy: opened by inline § codes. structural: opened by component fields (color/bold/italic/...). The distinction exists for the writer, not for the translator -- a person editing the file sees an opaque [[n]] either way.

sigma_expressible.description: True iff this segment's style can be written as legacy § codes inside a lang-file value. False for click_event, hover_event, font, insertion, and for nested translate nodes. A single false here forces unit.collapsible to false.

enforcement.description: Stays at warn for every category until the in-game font-width calibration lands. Enforcing an unverified budget would reject correct translations.

position.description: number, not integer: entity coordinates are doubles and text_display entities are routinely at non-integral positions.

occurrence.description: One physical location of this text. The write-back address, plus everything needed to rebuild the original component tree. The translation layer MUST NOT read this.

encoding.description: ★ AUTHORITATIVE. The shape actually found at this node, determined by sniffing the value -- NOT derived from container.data_version. [實測] DataVersion 4556 chunks in Minecraft Party 2 contain 2,340 json_empty_quoted and 110 json_string_object message elements, so DataVersion does not predict node shape. json_string_array is the ['', {...}, {...}] form (66 occurrences in 100 Ways To Die, 40 in Questioning). json_empty_quoted is the 2-character string '""'.

segment_styles.description: Style values for this occurrence, parallel to source.segments. segment_styles[n] is either {"codes": "§c"} for a legacy segment or the component's own formatting fields for a structural one. Style VALUES live here rather than on the unit so that the same sentence in gold and in red stays a single translation unit.

skeleton.description: The original component tree with every literal text replaced by its segment index. Required when encoding is compound_tree, json_string_object or json_string_array. This is what lets the writer rebuild a non-collapsible tree after translation; it is NOT 'verbatim carry-over'.

raw_snapshot.description: Byte-exact original value at this node, when it was a string. Used by the writer's expected-encoding guard to detect that the world changed under a stale plan.

excluded.description: Non-null means this occurrence MUST NOT appear in an edit plan. The exclusion is per-occurrence, not per-unit: the same source text can be real content in a DV 3955 chunk and display garbage in a DV 4556 one, so the unit is still translated and only the affected occurrences are held back.

reason.description: untested_write_shape: the unit is translatable and every other occurrence of it is writable, but for THIS node we have no game-tested answer for what shape to write. v1 holds it back rather than guessing. [實測] the case that introduced it is CustomName in a DV < 4325 chunk: DataFixerUpper parses that field there, so the native literal-string answer does not transfer, and an untested write path is more dangerous than refusing to write.

container.description: There is deliberately NO `generation` field. It used to be derived from data_version, and that derivation is now known to be wrong.

path.description: Relative to the world root, forward slashes.

data_version.description: This chunk's own DataVersion, used ONLY to write the chunk back at the generation it came from. It does NOT determine node encoding -- see occurrence.encoding. Null for chunks that predate the field entirely; such worlds are rejected by v1.

compression.description: Compression type as read, after masking off 0x80. Deliberately a plain integer rather than an enum: an unknown value must surface as UnknownCompressionError from parse_compression_byte, whose message names the offending value and chunk, not as a generic schema validation failure.

oneOf.description: Descend into a nested document encoded as a string at the current node. On write the writer re-encodes every decode level from the innermost outwards.

span.description: Byte offsets [start, end) inside the parent string. WARNING: when one parent string holds several translatable spans, editing any span invalidates the offsets of all later ones. The writer MUST apply same-parent edits in descending span order, or rebuild structurally instead of splicing.
